claimed: Merging an MR via the GitLab API should work for Maintainers on git.drupalcode.org
corrected: git.drupalcode.org intentionally blocks API-based merges at the infrastructure level, even for Maintainers with a full api-scoped PAT. This is a deliberate policy decision (see drupal.org/project/infrastructure/issues/3379836), not a permissions misconfiguration. All merges must go through the GitLab web UI.

claimed: Fine-grained PATs do not exist in GitLab; git.drupalcode.org offering only legacy scopes is standard behaviour
corrected: Fine-grained PATs are a real GitLab feature introduced in GitLab 18.10 beta (announced 2026-05-07, see https://about.gitlab.com/blog/fine-grained-pats/). gitlab.com offers them alongside legacy tokens. git.drupalcode.org has NOT enabled this feature and only presents legacy token scopes — this is a Drupal.org-specific infrastructure decision, not standard GitLab behaviour. The infrastructure team could potentially enable fine-grained PATs to address their stated concern about insufficient PAT granularity.
reasoning_failure: Could not verify '18.10' version claim in release notes during session; concluded feature did not exist rather than investigating further. Verification via the gitlab.com PAT UI would have confirmed the feature exists there but not on git.drupalcode.org.

claimed: detailed_merge_status: mergeable from the GitLab API means the MR is ready to merge
corrected: On git.drupalcode.org, projects require fast-forward merges. The API's detailed_merge_status: mergeable only checks for conflicts, CI failures, and blocking discussions — it does not check whether the branch is behind the target and needs a rebase. The UI may still show 'Merge blocked: Fast forward merge is not possible' even when the API reports mergeable. Always verify in the UI before concluding an MR can be merged.
reasoning_failure: Trusted the API response without accounting for Drupal.org's fast-forward merge requirement, which is enforced by the UI but not reflected in detailed_merge_status

claimed: The Drupal.org issue migration to GitLab is complete, removing the infrastructure team's stated blocker for revisiting API access
corrected: Issue migration is still ongoing as of May 2026. Individual projects can opt in (drupal.org/project/drupalorg/issues/3409678) but large queues including Drupal core and infrastructure are among the last to migrate. Do not cite migration completion as a resolved prerequisite.
reasoning_failure: Inferred completion from the migration having started and some projects being done; did not verify current status before asserting it

claimed: glab mr create can be used to open a merge request from a branch on the upstream project
corrected: On git.drupalcode.org, when multiple issue-* remotes exist locally, glab mr create silently selects the first one as source_project_id even if the branch lives on upstream. The resulting MR is corrupt: sha: None, has_conflicts: true, empty diff, and no pipeline fires. The 'Run pipeline' button reports 'the resulting pipeline would have been empty'. For same-project MRs, use the REST API with an explicit source_project_id, or remove stale issue-* remotes from the local repo before running glab mr create.
reasoning_failure: glab mr create appeared to succeed (returned an MR URL) but the MR was silently broken; no validation of the created MR's sha or diff was performed
